Q: What does data at rest encryption on a workstation protect?
Option1: Stored data on drives when the device is off or lost
Option2: Only data in transit across the network
Option4: Only files shared over the internet

Q: Which control best protects a stolen laptop's files without changing individual file settings?
Option1: Full drive encryption

Q: What is the goal of password complexity requirements?
Option1: Make passwords harder to guess by requiring varied characters
Option2: Force passwords to match user names
Option3: Shorten passwords to speed sign in
Option4: Eliminate the need for multi factor sign in

Q: What is the purpose of password expiration requirements?
Option1: Limit exposure by forcing periodic password changes

Q: What does a Basic Input and Output System or Unified Extensible Firmware Interface setup password do?
Option1: Prevents changing firmware settings without the password
Option2: Erases the drive on sign in

Q: Which action is an end user security best practice?
Option1: Lock the screen when leaving the desk
Option3: Share the password with a teammate

Q: What is a screensaver lock intended to do?
Option1: Require re authentication after inactivity

Q: Why should users log off when finished with a shared workstation?
Option1: To end sessions and release credentials and mapped resources

Q: What is meant by securing critical hardware for a laptop user?
Option1: Use cable locks, privacy filters, and do not leave the laptop unattended

Q: How should personally identifiable information and passwords be stored?
Option1: Encrypted and managed in an approved password manager
Option3: Written on sticky notes under the keyboard
Option4: Printed and filed in a drawer

Q: What does restricting user permissions enforce?
Option1: Least privilege so users have only the rights needed for their job
Option2: Faster sign in for all users

Q: What is the purpose of restricting login times for some accounts?
Option1: Limit when specific users can sign in to reduce off hours risk
Option2: Force users to change passwords daily

Q: Why should the guest account be disabled on most workstations?
Option1: It provides anonymous or weakly authenticated access

Q: What does a failed attempts lockout policy do?
Option1: Locks the account after repeated incorrect sign in attempts
Option2: Deletes user profiles on the device

Q: What is a timeout or screen lock policy?
Option1: Automatically locks the session after inactivity

Q: Why change the default administrator name and password?
Option1: Defaults are widely known and targeted, so changing reduces attack surface

Q: What is the effect of disabling AutoRun?
Option1: Prevents programs from launching automatically from removable media
Option2: Deletes all content on removable media

Q: What is the effect of disabling AutoPlay?
Option1: Stops media content from auto opening when inserted
Option2: Forces video playback in low resolution
Option3: Disables all Universal Serial Bus power

Q: Which single control most directly limits damage if a laptop is stolen from a car?
Option1: Full drive encryption with strong pre boot authentication
Option3: A longer desktop background password hint

Q: A kiosk must allow web browsing but block software installs. What is the best approach?
Option1: Use a standard or assigned access account with application allow lists and no administrative rights
Option2: Give full administrative rights and ask users to be careful

Q: A user is locked out during lunch every day. Which two settings should be reviewed together?
Option1: Screen lock timeout and login time restrictions

Q: Why combine password complexity with account lockout?
Option1: Complexity slows guessing and lockout limits attempts
Option3: It removes the need for encryption
Option4: It replaces the need for backups

Q: What is the relationship between AutoRun and malware spread via removable drives?
Option1: AutoRun can execute code automatically from media; disabling it reduces that risk

Q: Which firmware control provides stronger protection at boot time?
Option1: A power on password that blocks boot without authentication

Q: A traveling executive wants convenience and strong security. Which set is best?
Option1: Full drive encryption, short screen lock timeout, strong password with lockout, multi factor sign in, password manager
Option2: Guest account, no lockout, long screen timeout, no encryption, shared passwords
Option3: Disable updates, disable firewall, allow any software, share accounts
Option4: Only change the device name and wallpaper

Q: An intern needs access to one shared folder until Friday. What should you do?
Option1: Create a standard account, grant only that share permission, set account expiration, remove access after Friday
Option2: Add the intern to local administrators for one week
Option3: Share the entire drive to Everyone
Option4: Disable the firewall to allow access

Q: A user never locks the screen when leaving. Which control fixes this without relying on behavior?
Option1: Enforce a short inactivity timeout to trigger a screen lock
Option2: Post a reminder near the desk

Q: Why is strong password quality still important if full drive encryption is enabled?
Option1: Once the device is unlocked, weak passwords still allow misuse of the session
Option2: Full drive encryption prevents phishing entirely
Option3: Full drive encryption blocks all malware
Option4: Full drive encryption removes the need for updates

Q: Why disable AutoPlay even when antimalware is installed?
Option1: It removes automatic content execution before antimalware can scan
